notes: The patch walks the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect the literal names passed to `ph()`, marking the expression dynamic when a name isn't a literal, and then retries only on the agreed response placeholders: status_code/status_text, header.*, and the latency placeholders. This covers shorthand vs direct `ph()` calls, escaped literals, look-alike names and computed names; the new exported `Placeholders()` API on MatchExpression is a modest but justified surface addition, and the tests are thorough on both unit and end-to-end paths.

The fix walks the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect the literal names passed to `ph()`, and it treats non-literal names as dynamic. Only expressions that read status, header or latency placeholders become response conditions, which covers the shorthand and direct `ph()` forms, escaped literals, look-alike names and the dynamic-name case. It adds a small exported `Placeholders()` method on `MatchExpression`. Expressions nested inside `not` matchers are still not inspected, though the old code did not inspect them either.

Fixes both root causes. A reusable caller now refreshes to `cancelling` while a direct child is still `cancelling`, which carries up through nested callers. `cancelRun` also triggers `EmitJobsIfReadyByRun` when no job changed and the run is done. The tests cover nested callers through the runner ack and the force-cancel concurrency wake-up. Two weaknesses: the fix relies on `CancelJobs` cancelling children before their parents, and the emit condition does not check whether the run's status actually changed.

Fixes both parts of the issue: in `cancelOneJob`, a caller whose direct child is still cancelling now stays cancelling, and the status propagates up through nested callers via `RefreshReusableCallerStatus`; `cancelRun` now triggers the concurrency re-check when no job changed and the run is done. The fix depends on the order in which jobs are processed: it only checks direct children for `cancelling` at the moment the caller is visited, and relies on existing child-to-parent propagation for the other orderings rather than on a single invariant. Both tests are focused: the nested-caller acknowledgement test and the force-cancel test with a mocked emitter and a concurrency check.

Symlinks in zip and squashfs are hidden behind --links with a notice naming the flag, appear as .rclonelink objects sized to the target, read back the target with range/seek, and List and NewObject share one code path; the hostile case is handled by dropping clashing symlinks, case-insensitively, and the tests are thorough, but one hidden test fails, likely because the expected clash behaviour differs (it drops the symlink and keeps the member inside it, and drops clashing regular .rclonelink files), and NewObject on squashfs now reads every link target in the directory.

Adds `--links` symlink support to both the zip and squashfs backends, sharing `LinkFilter` and `OpenLink` helpers in the archiver package. It logs a notice naming the flag when links are skipped, honours range and seek options, and makes squashfs `NewObject` and `List` share one code path. A case-insensitive clash filter drops any symlink with a member beneath it, so a hostile archive cannot write outside the destination. One hidden test still fails, possibly because the clash semantics differ from what was expected, for example keeping the member and dropping the link rather than the reverse. Other weak points: it also hides regular `.rclonelink` files in clash cases, and it eagerly reads every zip symlink target at open time, which can be slow on remote storage such as S3.

The fix follows the maintainer design: `Close` is added to the interface, a failed field or table gather closes the cached connection, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, and reconnecting a closed v3 connection clears the engine ID, boots, time and localized keys so discovery runs again. Hidden PR tests pass, but it also rewrites the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (relative path plus `Log`) as an environment workaround, and the package suite fails for an unclear reason, which lowers confidence.

Implements the fix as the maintainers described: `Close` is added to the interface. Reconnecting a closed v3 session clears the engine ID, boots, time and localized keys so discovery runs again, while an open session is left alone. `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, and `Gather` closes the agent's connection after a field or table failure. Tests are solid. The patch also makes an unrelated, environment-driven change to `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (relative path plus an injected Log), and the package suite failed for an unclear reason.

The ref-counted unixSocket design looks sound on reading: it keeps one dup'd fd per socket, unlinks under a lock only while the socket is still the current map entry, guards double close with ErrClosed and skips unlink for abstract sockets. However, it reworks internal types (pointer-receiver deleteListener/deletePacketConn, new unixListener fields, a different unixSockets map type), and the hidden suite fails completely (0/7, package FAILED), so the fix is unverified and may break internal consumers.

The fix looks right on reading: one tracked dup per socket, a ref count guarded by a mutex, and unlink under the lock only when the last holder closes. It also handles double close with `ErrClosed` and skips abstract `@` sockets. But it restructures the internals heavily (the `unixSockets` map type, `unixListener` fields, and pointer-receiver `deleteListener`/`deletePacketConn`, which also changes TCP behaviour), and the package suite fails with 0/7 hidden tests passing; its own tests are thorough but cannot outweigh that.

Fixes the root cause in both places: a new `DiffPathPrefixes()` builder forces `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` on every lazygit-issued diff, including the worktree file diff that previously had no prefix forcing, and the parser now strips any single-component prefix, prefers `rename to`/`copy to`, and splits the `diff --git` line by matching halves; minor caveats are that other diffs such as stash show were not normalized and the name-status loader was touched where prefixes are irrelevant, with thorough unit tests plus an integration test.

Fixes the root cause on both fronts: any single-component header prefix is now stripped (with /dev/null kept and prefix-less paths resolving to empty), paths come from `rename to`/`copy to` first, the `diff --git` line is split where both halves match, and lazygit's own diff commands force `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`. Tests are thorough and cover mnemonic, quoted, space-containing and ambiguous paths; the minor drawbacks are that forcing a/b/ hides the user's mnemonic prefixes in displayed diffs, and some other call sites (e.g. stash show) may have been missed, which can't be confirmed from the truncated diff.

Fixes the root cause: it tracks each series' maximum exemplar timestamp (from commit, WAL replay and snapshot restore) and keeps exemplar-bearing series through both `gc` and `gcSeries` while releasing their in-order chunks, appender and mmap-ready accounting, and the thorough tests cover all three compaction paths, both appenders, snapshot restarts and zero/negative timestamps; minor costs are an extra 8 bytes on every `memSeries`, a per-exemplar lock in `commitExemplars`, and a new head test placed so it steals another test's doc comment.

Fixes the root cause: each series now tracks its max exemplar timestamp (set on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load), and both gc and gcSeries keep series whose exemplar is at or after minValidTime while releasing their chunks, appender and mmap-ready count. Downsides are 8 extra bytes per memSeries, a pending-commit bit taken for the flag, and a new head_test placed so it takes over TestHeadCompactionWhileAppendAndCommitExemplar's doc comment; the tests are otherwise thorough on paths, metrics, restarts and zero/negative timestamps.
